cells.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James prefers to recruit financial advisors one by one rather than through acquisitions, because 100% of transition assistance goes to retention of the advisor and the firm can ensure recruited advisors are a good cultural fit.
items.quote: we prefer to recruit 1 by 1 versus doing acquisitions because we know -- first, 100% of the transition assistance is going to retention of the adviser. And secondly, we can ensure that the advisers we're bringing over a really good cultural fits for the firm.

items.text: Raymond James does not lead with the highest check; it wants competitive economics but leads with culture and capabilities, and remains disciplined on transition assistance and economics.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check. We want to have competitive economics. Certainly, we have to have competitive economics, but we lead with culture and capabilities... we remain disciplined. We've always been disciplined on those transaction assistance -- transition assistance and economics to advisers.

items.text: Raymond James views recruiting as a consistent, long-term process that cannot be turned on and off quarter to quarter, focused on finding advisors who are good cultural fits across affiliation options.
items.quote: recruiting is not something you could turn on and off quarter-to-quarter. You can't -- you have to be consistent in that value proposition... having the team focused on finding advisers that are good cultural fits with the firm across our affiliation options.

items.text: Raymond James participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take and their ability to solicit clients when affiliating with a new firm.
items.quote: We participate, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting (“Protocol”), a voluntary agreement among many firms in the industry that governs, among other things, the client information that financial advisors may take with them when they affiliate with a new firm and the financial advisor’s ability to solicit clients of their prior firm.

items.text: Raymond James's recruiting approach includes collaborative recruiting across channels, a West Coast and Northeast geographic focus, and a next gen advisor strategy.
items.quote:
Collaborative recruiting across channels

West Coast and Northeast focus

Next gen advisor strategy

items.text: Raymond James builds its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor on a one-on-one basis.
items.quote: Shoukry has emphasized the firm's strategy of building its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, noting that the firm evaluates each prospective advisor on a one-on-one basis.

items.text: Raymond James has invested in its transition teams, giving them more capabilities and capacity to ensure seamless transitions of newly affiliated advisors while maintaining service to existing advisors.
items.quote: we have invested in the transition teams as well, given them more capabilities and capacities to really help with the uptake to ensure that we have seamless transitions of the new advisors, that are affiliating with the platform

items.text: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options (AdvisorChoice), allowing advisors to match their professional goals to the affiliation option right for them, which is central to its recruiting approach.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that’s right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: Raymond James develops new financial advisors through its Wealth Management Associate Program and Advisor Mastery Program, and has a dedicated department providing growth-oriented tools, resources and business coaching.
items.quote: Individuals who want to become financial advisors can gain relevant branch experience through our Wealth Management Associate Program or move to our Advisor Mastery Program and begin building their client base. We have a department dedicated to providing growth-oriented tools and resources, including business coaching, to our financial advisors.

cells.reason: The passages describe multiple facets of how Raymond James approaches advisor recruiting (one-by-one individualized recruiting, culture-and-capabilities-led positioning, consistency, Protocol participation, geographic and next-gen strategy, transition support, affiliation options, and advisor development programs), all of which are facts about the firm's recruiting approach.
